title: Software supply chain: would a poisoned package or action reach production?
short: Make new package versions wait 3 days, lock every GitHub Action to a commit and publish without long-lived tokens.
answer: This month, make new package versions wait three days before they install, lock every GitHub Action to a commit and replace long-lived publishing and cloud tokens with trusted publishing and OIDC. Judge every other control by whether it keeps credentials away from code you didn't write, or tells you within an hour where a bad version ran.
audience: Development, platform and DevOps teams that build and ship software, including small teams on GitHub

blocks.title: If you only do five things
blocks.intro: Third parties, including flaws in vendor software, were involved in 48% of the breaches in Verizon's 2026 DBIR, up 60% in a year[^dbir].

items.title: Make new versions wait three days.
items.text: Poisoned releases are often caught within hours: PyPI quarantined the LiteLLM and Telnyx ones within four hours of upload[^pypiinc]. Dependabot waits three days by default and pnpm one day[^dbdefault][^pnpmres]; set npm's `min-release-age=3`[^npmconfig] and a `P3D` cooldown in uv or pip[^pypiinc]. CISA suggested seven days after the axios compromise[^cisaaxios].

items.title: Block install scripts and install from the lockfile.
items.text: Shai-Hulud 2.0 ran from a `preinstall` script, before any test or security check[^msshai]. npm 12 blocks dependency install scripts by default and pnpm runs only approved ones[^npm12][^pnpmbuild]; approve the few that need it with `npm approve-scripts`[^npm12]. On older npm set `ignore-scripts=true`[^cisaaxios]. Commit lockfiles with hashes[^pypiinc] and install with `npm ci`.

items.title: Lock every action to a commit.
items.text: In March 2026 an attacker force-pushed 76 of 77 version tags of `trivy-action` to code that read secrets from runner memory[^trivy]. Turn on **Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA**, which a workflow lockfile satisfies, and set **Workflow permissions** to read-only[^ghsettings].

items.title: Publish and deploy without long-lived tokens.
items.text: GitHub calls removing long-lived credentials from CI/CD the number one thing you can do[^ghdisrupt]. Publish to npm and PyPI with trusted publishing[^npmtp][^pypiinc], set npm's **Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens**[^npmtp], delete the old tokens and deploy to clouds with OIDC[^secureuse]. Require phishing-resistant MFA on developer accounts[^cisaaxios].

items.title: Record what every build contained.
items.text: Generate an SBOM in the build for each release and keep it with the artifact[^cisasbom][^enisasbom], so you can tell within an hour whether you shipped a bad version. The CRA requires one from December 2027[^cra].

blocks.title: When a package or action you use is reported compromised

items.title: Did a bad version run anywhere?
items.text: Search lockfiles, caches and artifact registries, then CI pipelines and developer machines that installed packages in the exposure window[^cisaaxios]. OSV-Scanner checks lockfiles and SBOMs against OSV.dev[^osv], which includes OpenSSF's malicious-package (`MAL-`) records[^osvdata].

items.title: Is the machine still infected?
items.text: Isolate it before you revoke anything: Mini Shai-Hulud wipes the home directory if its GitHub token is revoked[^mitre]. Shai-Hulud 2.0 registered a GitHub Actions runner called `SHA1Hulud` on infected hosts[^msshai]. Remove persistence and rogue runners, or rebuild.

items.title: Which secrets could it reach?
items.text: Rotate every secret the job or machine could read, as CISA advises for a compromised CI run[^cisaaxios], and do it in one go: the Trivy attacker may have kept access because an earlier rotation wasn't atomic[^trivy].

items.title: What did the attacker do with them?
items.text: Look for new repositories (Trivy's payload created `tpcp-docs-` ones[^trivy]), workflow commits by automated accounts[^cisanx], versions you didn't publish and unusual cloud API calls.

items.title: Do you have to report it?
items.text: If malicious code could have reached a product you place on the EU market, treat it as a possible severe CRA incident, with an early warning due within 24 hours[^cra]. The EU security laws sheet has the other clocks.

blocks.title: If you place software on the EU market: the CRA
items: **Reporting applies now.** Since 11 September 2026, manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, also for products placed on the market before the rest of the CRA applies on 11 December 2027[^cra].
**A poisoned release counts.** An incident that has led or could lead to malicious code in your product or your users' systems is severe, such as malicious code in your update channel[^cra].

**The SBOM must be machine-readable, not public.** It needs a commonly used format, must cover at least top-level dependencies and goes to authorities on request; sharing it with users is optional[^cra]. CISA's 2026 minimum elements add transitive dependencies, hashes and licenses[^cisasbom].

**Vulnerability handling is due by December 2027.** Have a disclosure policy, a reporting contact, free security updates and public notes on fixed flaws for at least 5 years, or the expected use time if shorter. Report flaws in components to their maintainers[^cra].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Attacks moved into CI and release workflows.** Trivy's compromise spread through retagged actions in March[^trivy]. Mini Shai-Hulud scraped runner memory for identity tokens and swapped them for npm trusted-publisher tokens[^mitre]. In May CISA reported that a poisoned VS Code extension update led to theft of GitHub's internal repositories[^cisanx].
**Safer defaults shipped.** npm 12 blocks dependency install scripts and git and URL dependencies[^npm12][^npmconfig], and since July Dependabot waits three days before version updates[^dbdefault].

**GitHub Actions got lockfiles.** Since 28 October, `.github/workflows/actions.lock` pins actions to commits on Free, Team and Enterprise Cloud plans, and a **Require lockfile** policy enforces it[^lockga].
**npm is closing the token route.** Stage-only tokens hold a release until a maintainer approves it with 2FA, and npm aims to end direct publishing with bypass-2FA tokens in January 2027[^npmstage].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Chasing unreachable CVEs deep in the tree.** The CRA asks you to remediate in relation to the risks[^cra]. Fix exploited and reachable ones within the patching sheet's deadlines and batch the rest.

**Polishing SBOMs nobody reads.** Generate them in the build with tools you already have, as ENISA advises for a first implementation[^enisasbom]. Buy an SBOM platform only when a customer or regulator consumes them.
**SLSA Build L3 before the basics.** Close the moving tags, long-lived tokens and install scripts behind most 2026 incidents first.
**A registry proxy for a small team.** A cooldown, a lockfile and blocked install scripts give most of its benefit without the upkeep.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Publishing from a busy job.** Malware in the same job can read the OIDC token from runner memory[^mitre]. Publish from a separate job that installs nothing, in an environment that needs a reviewer's approval[^envs].

**Running fork code with secrets.** `pull_request_target` workflows are privileged, bypass fork approval and must not check out untrusted code[^secureuse][^ghsettings]. From 2 December GitHub blocks them in public repositories by default[^prt].

**Forgetting developer machines.** The poisoned Nx Console extension reached users through VS Code's automatic updates[^cisanx]. Allowlist extensions and pin approved versions with the `AllowedExtensions` policy[^vscode].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: In the organization's Actions settings, set read-only workflow permissions and require SHA-pinned actions or a lockfile.
Keep Dependabot's default cooldown and turn on Dependabot malware alerts, security updates and, where your plan includes it, secret scanning.
Move npm and PyPI publishing to trusted publishing, and run npm 12 or current pnpm in CI.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Add `.github/workflows` to CODEOWNERS and turn on **Require review from Code Owners**[^codeowners].
Publish from an environment with required reviewers and **Prevent self-review** (public repositories only on Free, Pro and Team)[^envs].
Scan lockfiles for malicious packages in every pull request with the OSV-Scanner action.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Route installs through a registry proxy that enforces a cooldown and checks for malware.
Attest builds with GitHub artifact attestations and verify them before deploy.
Keep each release's SBOM for 10 years or the support period, if longer[^cra], and add build pipeline compromises to your CRA reporting path.

changes.text: Published after a copy edit and a source-by-source fact check, which dated the CRA's SBOM duty to December 2027, made CODEOWNERS review enforceable and narrowed 8 statements to what the sources say.
